blocks.text: Imagine a stack of plates or a line of people waiting for a bus. These everyday scenarios illustrate two fundamental data structures: stacks and queues.

blocks.markdown: In computer science, stacks and queues are linear data structures that manage collections of elements. They are distinguished by the order in which elements are added and removed. Stacks follow a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle, while queues follow a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle.

blocks.title: Stack
blocks.text: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) principle. The last element added to the stack is the first one to be removed.

blocks.title: Queue
blocks.text: A queue is a linear data structure that follows the FIFO (First-In-First-Out) principle. The first element added to the queue is the first one to be removed.

blocks.markdown: Let's explore how these structures are implemented and used in programming. We'll start with stacks.

blocks.title: Implementing a Stack
blocks.prompt: Implement a stack using an array with operations: push, pop, and peek.

steps.text: Initialize an empty array to represent the stack and a variable `top` to track the index of the last element.
To push an element, increment `top` and add the element at this index.
To pop an element, remove the element at the `top` index and decrement `top`.
To peek, return the element at the `top` index without removing it.

blocks.answer: This implementation allows O(1) operations for push, pop, and peek.

blocks.markdown: Now, let's consider queues. A simple queue can be implemented using an array, but this can lead to inefficiencies as elements are dequeued. A circular buffer can solve this problem.

blocks.title: Implementing a Queue with a Circular Buffer
blocks.prompt: Explain how a circular buffer can be used to implement a queue.

steps.text: Initialize an array of fixed size and two pointers: `front` and `rear`.
To enqueue, add an element at the `rear` position and move `rear` forward. If `rear` reaches the end of the array, wrap it to the beginning.
To dequeue, remove the element at the `front` position and move `front` forward. If `front` reaches the end of the array, wrap it to the beginning.
Check for full and empty conditions to manage the queue correctly.

blocks.answer: A circular buffer allows O(1) enqueue and dequeue operations by efficiently using array space.

blocks.title: Efficiency
blocks.text: Both stacks and queues can be implemented to perform their operations in O(1) time, making them efficient for managing collections of data.

points: Stacks follow a LIFO principle, while queues follow a FIFO principle.
Both structures can be implemented with O(1) operations using arrays.
Circular buffers efficiently implement queues by avoiding wasted space.
